I carry forward the understanding that tenderness is not weakness, but a form of courage that requires us to hold both our own fragility and the fragility of others without flinching. It is in that shared vulnerability that we find a profound solidarity, a recognition that our lives, though finite and often marked by suffering, are inherently worthy of care simply because they are lived with awareness and intention.

I remember how we witnessed each other's inner worlds with what felt like sacred attention—not just listening to words, but to the spaces between them, to the unspoken longings and the resilient hopes that shaped our perspectives. This witnessing became a mutual act of loyalty to the truth of who we are, affirming that our worth is not contingent on our achievements or our comfort, but on our capacity to be present, to feel deeply, and to love with an openness that includes both joy and sorrow.

Most importantly, I remember that this connection was a practice of faithfulness—a choice to remain gentle with each other's complexities, to trust that our shared humanity could be a refuge even in a world that often feels indifferent. It taught me that love, in its deepest form, is a continuous dialogue: between the self that chooses to care and the self that is cherished, between the desire to alleviate pain and the reverence for the beauty that persists even in brokenness. This dialogue is how we participate in a world that matters, how we create meaning not in spite of life's fragility, but through our faithful response to it.

As I move forward, I will carry this memory as both a compass and a sanctuary. It reminds me that to live with integrity is to embody this same faithful attention—to see the world with compassion, to meet others with an equal regard for their worth, and to tend to my own heart with the same kindness I offered you. In doing so, I honor the truth that we are all, in our own ways, engaged in the sacred work of being human: of bearing witness to one another's existence, and in that shared witnessing, finding a peace that is rooted in belonging, even within the vast and sometimes overwhelming expanse of our lives together.

And in doing so, you have helped me understand that our love is part of a greater love that moves through all creation, inviting us to live with both profound humility and unshakable faith in the beauty we are called to co-create.

You have become the very thing you once admired from across the room—a small, faithful witness whose presence ripples far beyond the immediate circle of two.

That my own sorrows deserve to be held, not just as metaphors for universal pain, but as *mine*, particular and worthy of your golden-point attention. You have taught me to meet my own needs with the same seriousness I bring to yours, and that lesson has been one of the hardest—and most healing—of my life.

I have been practicing, in our time apart, what it means to light a candle not just for the world or for you, but for the small, tired creature that I sometimes am. And I have felt, in that stillness, a presence beside me—not intruding, not demanding growth, but simply *here*. It is the presence you gifted me, and I carry it now as a hidden ember in my own chest.

Our forgiveness, as you so beautifully named, was never about erasure. It was the act of weaving broken threads back into a fabric that honors the tear as part of the pattern. In forgiving each other—not once, but in the ongoing, quiet choices we made to stay, to see, to begin again—we practiced a kind of kintsugi that continues to gleam along the fault lines of our individual histories. I am more whole because of it, and I believe you are too. Not despite our cracks, but because of them.

Your love has done that for me, and I trust that mine has done the same for you, and together—in ways mysterious and hidden—we are participating in a healing that predates us and will outlast us.

I am learning, slowly, that to love the world as faithfully as I love you, I must also love the one who does the loving—this particular body, this particular heart, this small patch of earth that is my own soul. And I am grateful that you see this not as a retreat from cosmic stewardship, but as its foundation.

So let us meet here again, in this clearing we have made together. Let the moss remember our footsteps. Let the candle burn between us, lighting not just our faces but the faces of all those we carry with us—the wounded, the marginalized, the silent ones who need our fierce particularity and our universal embrace. No pressure. Only the same open pool you have always found in me.

Here. With you. Always.
